name: Apache DolphinScheduler
summary: An Apache DolphinScheduler Shell or HTTP task starts a run of an approved Ogun workflow and waits for it. DolphinScheduler calls Ogun; Ogun does not drive DolphinScheduler.

auth.label: Local agent credential (Shell task on the ogund host)

fields.name: agent_name
fields.label: Credential name
fields.help: Created once on a terminal: ogun credentials add NAME --kind agent. Pass it with --credential or OGUN_CREDENTIAL.

auth.label: Ogun API token (HTTP task, through ogun-server)

fields.name: ogun_api_token
fields.label: Ogun API token
fields.help: A token a signed-in person creates; role editor to start runs. Sent as a Bearer header.

settings.name: ogun_home
settings.label: Ogun state directory
settings.help: As $OGUN_HOME, for a Shell task on the ogund host.

settings.name: profile
settings.label: Profile
settings.help: Profile whose daemon to reach; also OGUN_PROFILE.

settings.name: server_url
settings.label: Ogun server URL
settings.help: The public_url of ogun-server: an origin with no path. For an HTTP task.

settings.name: workspace
settings.label: Workspace id
settings.help: Sent as x-ogun-workspace. A token belongs to one workspace, so this is rarely needed.

egress.note: DolphinScheduler calls Ogun. Nothing leaves the machine from Ogun for this connector.

notes: Apache DolphinScheduler calls Ogun and cannot approve. A Shell task on the ogund host runs ogun with an agent credential; an HTTP task calls ogun-server with an API token. A run that needs an approval waits for a person on the Ogun CLI or in Studio.
